**VA Law:** "A rental agreement shall not contain provisions that the tenant: Agrees to the exculpation or limitation of any liability of the landlord to the tenant arising under law or to indemnify the landlord for that liability or any associated costs" (VRLTA § 55.1-1208(A)(5))
**Source:** Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, § 55.1-1208(A)(5)
**Why it matters:** This clause purports to exempt the landlord from liability for injuries and property damage caused by fire, flood, water leaks, utility failures, and other maintenance-related hazards. **VA Law:** "The landlord shall: Make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition; Maintain in good and safe working order and condition all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning, and other facilities and appliances, including elevators, supplied or required to be supplied by him" (VRLTA § 55.1-1220(A)(2), (A)(4))

**Source:** Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, § 55.1-1204(I)
**Why it matters:** This clause permits the landlord to unilaterally change the rent amount during a holdover tenancy by notice alone, without the tenant's written consent. Virginia law requires both parties to consent in writing to any change in rental terms.
